\end{adjustbox}
\begin{tablenotes}\footnotesize
\item Local shoppers are split into random halves A and B (3 splits, averaged). Every comparison uses half A as the reference, so local and foreign data are compared against the same thing. Matched foreign = random foreign shoppers subsampled until they hold up to as many purchases of shared products as half B (median 647 vs 491; all foreign data: 1261); in 29\% of pairs the foreign data is smaller than half B and is used in full. Ratio = foreign agreement / local agreement, median over pairs; pairs with non-positive local agreement are excluded. Matched columns use fewer pairs where the matched sample is too small for the measure (5-nearest-neighbour overlap: 208 pairs). CIs: two-way cluster bootstrap over markets and categories.
\end{tablenotes}
